source_text:
Ἐὰν δέ τις ἰουδαϊσμὸν ἑρμηνεύῃ ὑμῖν, μὴ ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ. ἄμεινον γάρ ἐστιν παρὰ ἀνδρὸς περιτομὴν ἔχοντος χριστιανισμὸν ἀκούειν, ἢ παρὰ ἀκροβύστου ἰουδαῖσμόν. ἐὰν δὲ ἀμφότεροι περὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μὴ λαλῶσιν, οὗτοι ἐμοὶ στῆλαί εἰσιν καὶ τάφοι νεκρῶν, ἐφ̓ οἷς γέγραπται μόνον ὀνόματα ἀνθρώπων.
φεύγετε οὖν τὰς κακοτεχνίας καὶ ἐνέδρας τοῦ ἄρχοντος τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, μήποτε θλιβέντες τῇ γνώμῃ αὐτοῦ ἐξασθενήσετε ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ: ἀλλὰ πάντες ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ γίνεσθε ἐν ἀμερίστῳ καρδίᾳ.
εὐχαριστῶ δὲ τῷ θεῷ μου, ὅτι εὐσυνείδητός εἰμι ἐν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ἔχει τις καυχήσασθαι οὔτε λάθρα οὔτε φανερῶς, ὅτι ἐβάρησά τινα ἐν μικρῷ ἢ ἐν μεγάλῳ. καὶ πᾶσι δέ, ἐν οἷς ἐλάλησα, εὔχομαι, ἵνα μὴ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτὸ κτήσωνται.
thought_title: Reject Judaizing teaching and the ruler of this age
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Philadelphia, warning them against false teachers and urging unity.
pass_a_gloss: But if anyone interprets Judaism to you, do not listen to him. For it is better to hear Christianity from a man who has circumcision, than Judaism from an uncircumcised man. But if both do not speak about Jesus Christ, these are to me tombstones and graves of the dead, on which are written only names of men. Flee therefore the evil arts and the snares of the ruler of this age, lest being oppressed by his purpose you become weak in love. But all of you come together in the same place with an undivided heart. And I thank my God, that I have a good conscience among you and no one has anything to boast about, neither secretly nor openly, that I burdened anyone in small or in great matters. And for all, among whom I spoke, I pray, that they may not possess this as a testimony against them.

choices.why: Glossary term for the Jewish way of life that Ignatius says Christians must not follow
Glossary term for the devil, the ruler of this present age
The image is of grave markers inscribed only with human names, contrasting with living speech about Christ
Captures the sense of cunning, deceptive schemes of the devil
Emphasizes the unity of heart that Ignatius urges, matching his concern against division
In context, Ignatius prays that his words not become evidence used against those who heard him

pass_b_english: If anyone interprets Judaism for you, do not listen to him. It is better to hear Christianity from a man who has been circumcised than to hear Judaism from a man who has not. But if neither of them speaks about Jesus Christ, then to me they are tombstones and graves of the dead, on which only the names of human beings are written.

Flee, then, from the evil crafts and the snares of the ruler of this age, so that you may never be oppressed by his purpose and grow weak in love. Instead, all of you come together with an undivided heart.

I thank my God that I have a good conscience among you, and no one can boast, either secretly or openly, that I burdened anyone in small things or in great things. And for all those to whom I spoke, I pray that my words may not become testimony against them.

last_rejected.why: Brief glosses θηριομαχία as 'martyrdom by beasts'; κακοτεχνίας means 'evil devices/crafts', not 'evil arts' specifically.
last_rejected.ruling: κακοτεχνίας = 'evil arts/crafts/devices' are all within normal range; 'arts' is acceptable.

last_rejected.quote: so that you may never be oppressed by his purpose
last_rejected.why: γνώμη means 'mind/plan' not 'purpose'; 'oppressed by his purpose' is awkward and unclear.
last_rejected.fix: so that you may never be crushed by his mindset
last_rejected.ruling: γνώμη can mean 'purpose/intent'; rendering is within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: ἐξασθενήσετε means 'become weak/give out', but 'grow weak in love' misses that love is the sphere where weakness shows.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ naturally denotes sphere; 'grow weak in love' conveys this adequately.

last_rejected.quote: that they may not acquire it as testimony against them
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτὸ κτήσωνται
last_rejected.why: αὐτὸ refers back to Ignatius's speech/words; 'acquire it' is unclear. They should not 'hold it against themselves' as witness.
last_rejected.fix: that they may not take it as testimony against themselves
last_rejected.ruling: αὐτὸ refers to preceding speech; 'acquire it as testimony' is intelligible, not a major error.

problems.quote: If anyone expounds Judaism to you, do not listen to him. For it is better to hear Christianity from a circumcised man than Judaism from an uncircumcised man.
problems.why: The wording suggests a literal preference for circumcision status, which misrepresents Ignatius’ likely polemic against Judaic legalism.
problems.fix: Rephrase: “Better to receive Christianity from those who have embraced it fully than Judaism from those who reject Christ.”

problems.quote: they are to me tombstones and graves of the dead
problems.why: 'Tombstones and graves' may be too literal; the point is spiritual deadness.
problems.fix: Consider 'monuments of death' or explain the metaphor.

edits.old: For it is better to hear Christianity from a circumcised man than Judaism from an uncircumcised man.
edits.new: For it is better to hear Christianity from a man who has circumcision than Judaism from an uncircumcised man.

edits.old: they are to me tombstones and graves of the dead
edits.new: they are to me monuments of death

fixed: The first problem is not a mistranslation: the source literally contrasts a circumcised man with an uncircumcised man, and the English already says this. No change needed.
The second problem is valid: 'tombstones and graves of the dead' is too literal. Changed to 'monuments of death' to convey spiritual deadness.

problems.quote: I pray that they may not acquire it as testimony against them
problems.why: 'Acquire it' has no clear antecedent; pronoun reference is lost.
problems.fix: Clarify what 'it' refers to, e.g., 'acquire this as testimony against them.'

edits.old: I pray that they may not acquire it as testimony against them.
edits.new: I pray that they may not acquire this as testimony against them.

fixed: Changed 'acquire it' to 'acquire this' to clarify the pronoun reference, matching the source's demonstrative sense.

problems.quote: It is better to hear Christianity from a man who has been circumcised than to hear Judaism from one who has not.
problems.why: Paradox is point, but 'hear Christianity from a circumcised man' vs 'Judaism from uncircumcised' is compressed; reader may miss that 'circumcised' means Jewish Christian.
problems.fix: Expand: 'better to hear Christian teaching from a Jewish Christian than Jewish teaching from a Gentile'.

fixed: The English already says the same thing as the source; the suggested expansion would add interpretation not required by the Greek.

problems.why: 'Evil arts' in 5.6, 7.5 likely translates same root as 'magic' in 1.19 (pharmakeia/mageia), but reader cannot connect these.
problems.fix: Use consistent translation or cross-reference in notes.

problems.quote: It is better to hear Christianity from a man who has been circumcised than to hear Judaism from one who has not.
problems.why: Paradox is point, but 'hear Christianity... than hear Judaism' with circumcision status reversed is easy to misread as error.
problems.fix: Add note: deliberate paradox—value of speaker depends on message, not ethnic identity.

Changed 'evil arts' to 'evil crafts' to avoid confusion with the magic-related term in 1.19, since the source here is κακοτεχνίας (evil crafts), not φαρμακεία/μαγεία.

fixed: The source reads 'παρὰ ἀνδρὸς περιτομὴν ἔχοντος... ἢ παρὰ ἀκροβύστου' — literally 'from a man having circumcision... than from an uncircumcised man.' The English 'from one who has not' is too compressed and unclear; the contrast between 'a man who has circumcision' and 'an uncircumcised man' should be explicit. Changed 'from one who has not' to 'from an uncircumcised man' to match the source's ἀκροβύστου.
